background.title: Background
background.p1: I work where business workflows meet software: CRMs, ERP modules, customer apps, and the glue that keeps them coherent. Less framework theater, more systems people can run every day.
background.p2: The path ran through open banking in Ottawa, logistics automation, React Native, IoT, Python teaching, and now a steady load of Dakar client work alongside Everest Finance and ERGOBIT.

01.name: Everest Finance
01.desc: Public site, internal CRM, and customer app on one TypeScript stack and shared Postgres schema.
01.detail: Marketing, CRM, and the customer app had drifted apart. I brought them onto one codebase and database so ops and product do not fight separate sources of truth.
01.outcomes:
One schema behind web, CRM, and mobile
Shipped public site, then CRM, then app hardening
Shared validation from marketing through transactions

02.name: ERGOBIT / Odoo 18
02.desc: Acceptance-test kit for Odoo 18 migrations—39 tests, nine suites, CI on Azure DevOps.
02.detail: Each migration team was rebuilding selectors from scratch. I packaged Robot Framework and Playwright patterns with CI so the next project starts from a checklist, not a blank repo.
02.outcomes:
39 acceptance tests in nine suites
Azure DevOps runs on every change
Selector notes that survive small UI drift

03.name: Africa GreenTec accounting
03.desc: Accounting module that removed most manual journal work—about 10k lines a day in production.
03.detail: Finance was keying the same patterns every day. The module encodes those flows, checks against operational data, and keeps a clear audit trail without spreadsheet bridges.
03.outcomes:
Most recurring entries automated
~10k records per day in production
Exports ready for management reports

04.name: BocalBun retrospective
04.desc: A Bun toolkit I paused when the abstractions cost more than they saved.
04.detail: I tried a Bun-native toolkit with Postgres RLS and strict layers. Delivery slowed, so I stopped and wrote up what was worth keeping—a better outcome than a quiet repo.
04.outcomes:
Architecture and schema documented before pause
Clear notes on when to resume or drop it
Public write-up instead of a zombie project

approach.title: Start from the workflow, not the framework.
approach.lead: The useful work is often less glamorous than the architecture: a reliable CRM state transition, a migration test that catches regressions, a CI pipeline that saves a team from manual checking.

principles.p2: A system is done when someone can operate it.
principles.p3: Architecture should reduce drift, not impress engineers.
principles.p4: Use AI to increase throughput without losing ownership.

AboutPage.title: About
AboutPage.name: Aliou Wade
AboutPage.bio: I build operational software: internal tools, CRM consolidation, ERP modules, and customer-facing apps. Recent work spans Everest Finance (fintech), ERGOBIT (Odoo), and contracts with BankingBook Analytics and Purolator. I work in French and English from Dakar.
AboutPage.context: I play chess — not competitively, but it shapes how I think about systems: patience, positional tradeoffs, playing the long game. I came up as an operator, not an academic. I've run a bakery logistics chain, built carpooling coordination tools, and shipped software that businesses depend on daily. That operational context is what I bring to every system I build.
